Company Description
Glow Health Care Australia is a healthcare provider delivering services across aged care, disability support, community care and other healthcare settings. We are seeking a full-time Enrolled Nurse to provide safe, person-centred nursing care to clients in accordance with care plans, professional standards and organisational policies. The role involves supporting clients across a variety of care settings and working collaboratively with Registered Nurses and other healthcare professionals to ensure high-quality service delivery.
Position Summary:
We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Enrolled Nurse to join our team with a primary focus on conducting client assessments in community and aged care settings. This role is ideal for a nurse who is confident working independently and has strong clinical judgment and communication skills.
Key Responsibilities
· Provide nursing care to clients in accordance with care plans, clinical instructions and accepted nursing practice
· Implement nursing interventions, treatments and therapies within scope of practice
· Administer medications where appropriately endorsed and authorised
· Monitor clients’ responses to treatment and care and report changes in condition to the supervising Registered Nurse or relevant clinical staff
· Observe, record and report symptoms, behaviours and changes in clients’ health and wellbeing
· Assist Registered Nurses and other healthcare team members in the coordination and evaluation of care provided to clients
· Support the implementation and review of care plans under the direction of a Registered Nurse
· Provide support to clients with activities of daily living, including mobility, hygiene, nutrition and comfort, where required
· Maintain accurate, timely and complete clinical documentation in accordance with organisational requirements
· Communicate effectively with clients, families, carers and members of the multidisciplinary team
· Participate in handovers and provide relevant clinical information to support continuity of care
· Promote client dignity, independence and choice in the delivery of care
· Support health, wellbeing and safe care practices in accordance with client needs and care plans
· Comply with organisational policies and procedures, including infection control, medication management, privacy and workplace health and safety requirements
· Participate in required training, supervision and continuous quality improvement activities
Skills and Qualifications:
· Diploma or equivalent qualification leading to registration as an Enrolled Nurse in Australia
· Current registration as an Enrolled Nurse with AHPRA
· At least 2-3 years of experience in a relevant nursing position
· Medication endorsement, where applicable
· Strong clinical observation, communication and documentation skills
· Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team
· Current CPR and First Aid certification
· National Police Check
· NDIS Worker Screening Check, or willingness to obtain one
How to apply
Don't miss out on this unique and rewarding nursing adventure.
Please Click APPLY FOR THIS JOB and one of our dedicated consultants will be in contact with you to discuss further.
Alternatively, contact us on email josephine.n@ghca.com.au

Full Time Registered Nurse
Address : Lot 342 – 8 Terone Street, Halls Creek, WA 6770

Position Summary
The Practice Nurse plays a key role within the clinic, delivering a high standard of quality nursing care through efficient, effective, safe, and timely services to YYMS patients. The nurse exercises a significant level of initiative in coordinating, implementing, and monitoring patient care, ensuring appropriate clinical outcomes. 

With a strong primary health care focus, the Practice Nurse works collaboratively with other members of the multidisciplinary team to implement preventative health strategies, provide therapeutic interventions, and deliver health promotion and education sessions. The position supports clinical operations and contributes to the overall functioning of the clinical service. 

Key Responsibilities 

Clinical Care & Assessment 
•	Triage patients and provide emergency management where required. 
•	Conduct holistic health assessments, including patient history, health screening, physical examinations, and preventative health checks. 
•	Support and promote the integration of STI testing into routine primary health care, including adult health checks. 
•	Administer immunisations in accordance with current guidelines. 
•	Perform clinical duties within the nurse’s level of competency and scope of practice, following best available evidence. 
•	Apply nursing assessment skills and practice safely and professionally, aligned with standards and guidelines. 
•	Work with Medical Practitioners to plan, coordinate, and manage patient care. 
•	Asist Medical Practitioners during clinical procedures. 
•	Provide therapeutic care and treatment, including: 
o	COVID support and management 
o	Wound care 
o	Minor surgical procedure assistance 
o	Medication and Vaccine administration 

Diagnostic & Clinical Support Services 
•	Conduct diagnostic tests such as ECGs, stress tests, hearing checks, spirometry, drug screening, mental health assessments (mood and memory), and other approved procedures. 
•	Refer clients to appropriate support groups and community services when needed. 
•	Deliver services that meet Integrated Team Care Program Guidelines. 

Patient Experience, Cultural Safety & Community Engagement 
•	Deliver welcoming, respectful, and professional services for all clients. 
•	Maintain fairness, confidentiality, equity, and a safe environment for diverse populations. 
•	Provide culturally appropriate care, incorporating feedback from Aboriginal Health Workers and other Aboriginal staff. 
•	Practice using a holistic view of Indigenous health. 
•	Build culturally sensitive health plans that support client ownership and self-determination. 
•	Provide outreach services including home visits, school visits, and community visits when required. 

Leadership, Collaboration and Education 
•	Provide leadership in nursing and primary healthcare principles. 
•	Collaborate effectively with the practice team and communicate with external providers and referrers. 
•	Provide health assessments, health promotion, quality improvement, and population health education. 
•	Provide training, mentorship, and support to Aboriginal Health Workers. 
•	Organise case conferences and multidisciplinary meetings as required.

Clinical Administration and Documentation
•	Maintain accurate, timely, and clinically appropriate patient documentation in accordance with policy and procedures. 
•	Collect and enter clinical data into the MMEx system to support complete medical records and accurate reporting. 
•	Optimise Medicare claiming in accordance with program requirements. 
•	Manage clinical supplies and resources in line with organisational policy. 
•	Oversee infection control procedures, patient flow, and clinical processes. 

Care Coordination and Client Support 
•	Work with clients and team members to identify and address broader needs (e.g., accommodation, financial support, wellbeing). 
•	Facilitate access to essential allied health or specialist services, transport, and GP-approved medical aids. 
•	Appropriately utilise supplementary services funding for eligible clients. 
 

Selection Criteria 

Essential:
•	Demonstrated ability as a Registered Nurse in Aboriginal Primary Health Care, including clinical and emergency practice in a remote setting. 
•	Demonstrated knowledge and skills in primary health care, COVID-19 management, vaccinations, and health education/promotion/prevention programs. 
•	Demonstrated ability to positively interact with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people to achieve community-desired outcomes. 
•	Demonstrated understanding of rural and remote health issues, including personal strategies for managing stress. 
•	Demonstrated understanding of cultural safety and its application in clinical and community settings. 
•	Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team, partnering with internal and external service providers. 
•	Demonstrated knowledge of Standards of Clinical Practice. 
•	National Police Clearance (or willingness to obtain).

Desirable: 
•	Current “C” Class Driver’s Licence. 
•	Working knowledge and understanding of relevant legislative Acts that impact the organisation and associated accountabilities. 
•	Local Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person. 
•	Fully COVID-19 vaccinated (evidence required) 

Applications open on 4 March 2026 and close on 3 April 2026.

We offer an unwavering commitment to provide the community with the best in residential aged care services. 

We are looking for an experienced Registered Nurseto join our amazing team.  

Key Responsibilities 

?  Assess, plan, implement, and evaluate nursing care for patients with acute and chronic medical conditions, including complex cardiac disorders. 

?  Perform comprehensive physical and clinical assessments, interpret diagnostic results, and identify actual and potential health problems. 

?  Develop and implement evidence-based nursing care plans in consultation with patients, families, and the multidisciplinary healthcare team. 

?  Provide specialised nursing care for patients with cardiovascular conditions, including post-myocardial infarction, heart failure, arrhythmias, and those requiring continuous cardiac monitoring. 

?  Administer prescribed medications, including intravenous therapies and cardiac-specific pharmacological treatments, and monitor patient responses for therapeutic effectiveness and adverse reactions. 

?  Monitor and interpret cardiac telemetry, vital signs, and clinical indicators to detect deterioration and initiate appropriate interventions. 

?  Prepare and support patients undergoing diagnostic and interventional procedures, including electrocardiograms, stress testing, echocardiography, and cardiac catheterisation. 

?  Maintain accurate and timely documentation of assessments, interventions, clinical observations, and patient outcomes in accordance with professional and legal standards. 

?  Provide health education and counselling to patients and families regarding disease processes, treatment regimens, medication management, lifestyle modification, and discharge planning. 

?  Collaborate with medical practitioners and allied health professionals to ensure coordinated, safe, and effective patient care. 

?  Implement infection prevention and control measures and comply with workplace health and safety requirements. 

?  Participate in quality improvement activities, clinical audits, risk management processes, and continuing professional development to maintain clinical competence.
